column1: # PB-RUN-3 -- the foreground/background connectivity policy, as a table rather than prose.
# Prose cannot be checked for totality, and the failure this requirement exists to prevent is
# not a wrong decision but an UNSTATED one. android/gate/connectivity_test.go enforces that
# every condition PB-RUN-3 names has a row, that every cell comes from a closed vocabulary,
# and that the rows are jointly consistent. ConnectivityPolicyTest.kt asserts the shipping
# implementation IS this table.
# The decision itself is ADR-007 B16: backgrounding DISCONNECTS and no foreground service
# ships in v1. B7's inbound mechanism parks a socket in a bounded server-side wait for up to
# 25 s (docs section 6.0), which is exactly what Doze, App Standby and battery saver exist to
# kill. Holding it would force a foregroundServiceType of dataSync (capped from API 34 at
# ~6 h/day, after which the system force-stops the service) or specialUse (a Play-review
# dependency on a personal tool). Dropping it makes the high-priority FCM wake in
# android/fcm-priority.tsv load-bearing, which is what D6 already assumed.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   state               foreground | background | doze | app_standby | battery_saver
#   socket              connected | suspended | closed
#   max_wait_s          ceiling on a server-side wait ISSUED in this state; 0 = none
#   foreground_service  yes | no
#   fgs_type            an Android foregroundServiceType token, or - when there is no service
#   wake_path           socket | push | none -- how the machine reaches the phone here
#   wait_on_entry       keep | cancel -- what happens to an ALREADY-OUTSTANDING wait on entry
foreground
background
doze
app_standby
battery_saver
